title: [Stable C Shim] Add new/delete function for StableIValue
body:
## Issue
- Pytorch Stable ABI support; https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/174507#issuecomment-4150977835

## Summary
Quote from the linked issue describes the problem:

> When I got around to implementing [to](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/21b62de20398cf05cb814f48eeb505ad1a777ba5/torch/csrc/stable/ops.h#L824) I needed to handle the `std::optional<T>` types on the rust side, in [stableivalue_conversions.h](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/21b62de20398cf05cb814f48eeb505ad1a777ba5/torch/csrc/stable/ops.h#L824) is an innoculous looking `new StableIValue`, that value is then freed by the dispatcher (appreciate the detailed comment above that specialisation!). Tricky part is that on the rust side I can't do a c++ `new StableIValue`, I can call `malloc`, but that's not the same as `new` and valgrind rightfully points out the mismatch. Ideally, for interop, the side that allocates a value should free it, because they may have a different memory allocator. I propose adding a method to create a new StableIValue on the heap, something like; 3b4f291416ecf7c66b4f08f7ffa95ffeca2f928d and using that instead of `new StableIValue`.

@janeyx99 nudged me towards a PR in [this comment](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/174507#issuecomment-4178953697). In this PR the problem is solved with two new functions:

- `AOTITorchError aoti_torch_new_stable_ivalue(StableIValue** ret_value);` to allocate a StableIValue on the heap.
- `AOTITorchError aoti_torch_delete_stable_ivalue(StableIValue* value);` to free the allocation again.

This ensures that the value cleared by `to_ivalue()` can be allocated correctly through the C shim.

As an alternative I considered the generalisation of always allocating an array of StableIValues, something like;
```c
aoti_torch_new_stable_ivalues(StableIValue** ret_value, size_t count);
```
Which has the benefit that if a StableIValue representation is created that requires multiple values the same allocation function can be used, and a single value can still be allocated by passing a count of 1. But then I realised that this doesn't work, because the `new StableIValue` is already part of the ABI, and we can't call `delete[]` on it, it must be `delete` for valgrind to be happy, so that ship has sailed.


New unit test was added for these functions and the functions `from_ivalue` and `to_ivalue` were updated to use the newly created allocation functions to ensure consistency.

The unit tests are currently in a new directory and file. The test directories don't appear to mirror the directory structure of the code. I looked through the test directories in depth to find an existing place I could add to before making a new directory;
- Currently it appears that the stable API is mostly tested through the [libtorch_agn_2_*_extension](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/tree/43eaba0456680ba31f758708cc944aea029c6f0d/test/cpp_extensions/libtorch_agn_2_11_extension) extension tests, but I thought a pure cpp / gtest was more appropriate for these changes.
- I copied the CMakeLists from [aoti_inference](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/tree/main/test/cpp/aoti_inference). It felt like a lot of boilerplate, its neighbouring directory; [aoti_eager](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/tree/43eaba0456680ba31f758708cc944aea029c6f0d/test/cpp/aoti_eager) doesn't even have a CMakeLists.txt and `rg kernel_meta_info_test` doesn't result in any hits (it also doesn't make any executable binary in my build dir), so not sure if that's a bug, or I'm missing something.
- Conceptually, it would make sense to be with [aoti_abi_check](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/tree/43eaba0456680ba31f758708cc944aea029c6f0d/test/cpp/aoti_abi_check), but the readme there states that's for the headeronly code.


## Checklist

- [x] Passes lint (`spin fixlint`) -> Yes, it added two functions unmodified by this PR to  `shim_function_versions.txt` which were previously missing.
- [x] Added/updated tests -> I added them, including a new directory for `aoti_torch`, I wasn't sure where to put them, happy to move them around.
- [x] Updated documentation (if applicable)
- [x] Included benchmark results (for PRs impacting perf)-> Valgrind output of new test below.

items.author: iwanders
items.body: The `STABLE_SHIM_USAGE` lint raised that I was using a versioned function without having a version guard around it. It feels a bit odd to me, given that the code change here is accompanied by the new functions, but I presume it has to do with the testing of all possible `TORCH_VERSION` defines from the unit tests.
